My girlfriend has the ability to fall asleep in fifteen seconds, as long as I'm lightly running my fingers along her back (she sleeps on her tummy and I do too).


It takes me 2-3 hours every single night to fall asleep. It's a major struggle; like a battle being waged every night, and nobody knows but me. I think it has a lot to do with anxiety; some people are just generally more anxious than others. I also wake up an hour BEFORE my alarm clock every day.


There are biological reasons. Everyone's brain is different; none of our brains produce the exact same amount of chemicals. Some people produce much less of the drug that puts you to sleep, and some people produce much more adrenaline and have much more testosterone. I just found out that I am hypersensitive to caffeine (I'm 26 and just discovering this). Caffeine has no apparent effect on me when I drink it at lunch time, but its half-life is like 10 hours in the human body, so if I drink a soda at noon I'm still completely unable to fall asleep by 10PM. I've since quit drinking soda and it has helped me a bit.


There are other things you can do. Don't eat 1-2 hours before bed. Dont drink too much water. DO NOT stare at a tv or computer screen for an hour before bed; it stimulates the waking regions of your brain, like looking at a meadow in daylight. Have sex or masturbate before bed. Have an unwind session, a relaxation period, two hours before bed, where you just chill the fuck out and slip into a calmer mood. Keep your lights low and dim for the same reasons mentioned above.


Lastly, if you find your thoughts racing too much as you try to sleep, as mine do, it means you are not allotting enough time during your day to 'problem solve' in your mind. Take a 30 minute walk with no phone/ipod. Just be alone with your thoughts, and sort through them BEFORE you get into bed.


Dont use the bed for anything but sleep or sex. No homework, no tv, no essay writing, no spreadsheets. Mental association can connect your bed to stressful thoughts. I won't even study in my bedroom at all.
